gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its $129.99 middle pick, the TESmart HKS201-P23, is limited to 100 Hz on a 3440×1440 ultrawide (4K at 60 Hz, 1440p at 120 Hz, 1080p at 240 Hz). They also don't say that its premium pick, the StarTech D86A2 DisplayPort 1.4 KVM, runs a 5120×1440 super-ultrawide at only 60 Hz and needs DSC to reach its 4K 144 Hz / 8K 60 Hz maximums.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. DeskDNA (deskdna.com/gear/monitors/best-kvm-switch) gives UGREEN HDMI limits of 4K@60, 1440p@120 and 1080p@240, and its TESmart pick is a different DisplayPort 1.4 model. It never mentions the HKS201-P23, ultrawide refresh caps or a DSC requirement. iTechGuides (itechguides.com) covers the StarTech SV211DPUA4K (DP 1.2), DSC only for Level1Techs, and the missing EDID and hotkeys only for UGREEN's 2-monitor listing. It covers neither the HKS201-P23 nor the StarTech D86A2. So the rivals have the general HDMI-vs-DP point and some EDID and hotkey facts, but not these model-by-model ultrawide and DSC limits. I could not open the other ten top results because of the call budget and rate limits.
decides: It confirms the HDMI pick for a 16:9 monitor at 4K 60 Hz or lower. On TESmart's own page, the HKS201-P23 also lists EDID emulation (windows don't rearrange on a switch) and switching by keyboard hotkey or mouse wheel, which justifies its price over a basic button switch. It changes the pick for ultrawide owners. A 3440×1440 monitor rated above 100 Hz loses refresh rate on the HKS201-P23. A 5120×1440 high-refresh monitor is held to 60 Hz even on the $450-plus StarTech, and that unit's 4K 144 Hz claim depends on DSC support. Both computers also need DisplayPort output.
